newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sees new hope for bipartisan budget accord.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sees new hope for bipartisan budget accord.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday the bipartisan cooperation that led to Senate approval of the chemical weapons treaty convinced him that a balanced-budget accord is also attainable and "we will do it."

"If we proceed as we did in the chemical weapons agreement, I'm convinced that we can (get a White House-Congress agreement on a balanced budget)," Clinton said at a joint news confernce with Japan's Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto. "I think its so manifestly in the interest of the United States that we do this ... that we will do it."

"Just as we didn't have the votes on the chemical weapons convention, we found the votes to do it because it was in the national interest," Clinton said. He commented one day after the Republican-led Senate handed him a major foreign policy breakthrough, handily approving a worldwide pact banning chemical weapons that once seemed doomed to rejection.

The Democratic president announced at the outset of his news conference with Hashimoto that he had just signed the document formally ratifying the Senate action and making the United States a participant in the treaty.

He said the whole process of bipartisan give-and-take on that issue convinced him a similar effort would produce a breakthrough in talks to reach accord on a balanced federal budget by 2002. He conceded that Republicans want less spending and more tax cuts in the mix than he does.
He said he was confident agreement would be reached "sometime this year" at the least but added, "I favour an early balanced budget agreement."
